newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares fall on MOL report.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares fall on MOL report.

text.p: Hungarian shares continued to fall on Thursday as the earnings report of oil and gas company MOL increased uncertainty on the market after the Wall Street's losses on Thursday and the forint's rise against the dollar overnight, traders said.
The BUX index of the Budapest Stock Exchange closed at a preliminary 7,741.75 points, down 74.51 points.
Traders said market sentiment remained uncertain after the recent downward price corrections following sharp rises earlier in the year.
"In a situation like this, negative news push the market further down," said Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings.
MOL said in its earnings report published Thursday morning, that it posted a net income of 12.545 billion forints in the first half of the year.
This result was below the expectations of many market players by billions of forints, traders said.

"This result was rather bad," said Robert Stalmayer of brokerage AB-Moneta, adding that MOL opened sharply down due to the news, than began to recover later in the session but closed down by 120 forints, at 4,400 forints.
Traders added that most other shares followed MOL.
They said the downtrend may continue in the next few days, especially if the Dow index does not recover and the forint remains relatively strong versus the dollar.
"The Dow weighs much and if it continues to go down, we will probably go down, too," Stalmayer said, adding, however that the market remained optimistic for the longer term.
